title: Lift Equation
learningObjectives: Calculate lift from lift coefficient, air density, velocity, and wing area
Explain how the lift coefficient collects shape, inclination, viscosity, and compressibility effects

evidence.quote: lift L is equal to the lift coefficient Cl times the density rho times half of the velocity V squared times the wing area A.

explanations.text: Lift equals the lift coefficient times density times half the velocity squared times wing area.

evidence.quote: For lift, this variable is called the lift coefficient, designated "Cl."
This allows us to collect all the effects, simple and complex, into a single equation.

explanations.text: The lift coefficient is a single variable that collects simple and complex effects into one equation.

evidence.quote: "density times the square of the velocity divided by two" is called the dynamic pressure and appears in Bernoulli's pressure equation.

explanations.text: Density times velocity squared divided by two is called dynamic pressure.

predictions.prompt: Predict the lift for a wing with Cl 0.6 at 60 m/s with sea-level air density and 15 m2 wing area.
Predict the lift for a wing with Cl 1.0 at 40 m/s with air density 1.0 kg/m3 and 20 m2 wing area.
